newsitem.title: FRANCE: France ends public sector company wage fixing.
newsitem.headline: France ends public sector company wage fixing.

text.p: The office of French Prime Minister Alian Juppe said on Tuesday that he had decided to end a 14-year old practice of fixing a ceiling for wage increases at public sector companies.
A source in Juppe's office said Juppe had made the decision because the increasing diversity among France's industries made across-the-board wage rises for all public companies impractical.

It was "preferable to set the framework for the wage policy company-by-company to better take into account the specific financial situation and the environment, monopolistic or competitive, in which they operate," the source said.

French newspapers said the practice, in which the prime minister sent letters to each ministry detailing the maximum allowable rise in wages at companies under their supervision, tended to push unions to aim for the upper limit of the range when they negotiated.
The move will have an impact on salary negotiations affecting about one million workers at some 100 companies in which the state controls at least 50 percent.
Employees at France Telecom and La Poste will not be affected, as more than 90 percent of them are civil servants.
The practice therefore ended up having the effect of all but setting the level of wage increases, not of setting a theoretical ceiling as the government intended.
Financial daily Les Echos said Juppe was ending the tradition of sending the letters to other ministers.
Since the government may skip salary negotiations with civil servants it would be difficult to announce plans for a wage increase for employees of state-owned companies, Les Echos reported.
Afternoon daily Le Monde reported that unions and management at public sector companies welcomed the news.
"From now on, wage policy will no longer depend on an average but on the performance of each company," the paper quoted an official at power utility group EDF-GDF as saying.
